cards.head: China's leaders told officials not to pour money blindly into AI and high tech.
cards.body: New guidelines from the ruling party and cabinet warn against swarm-like rushes into high-tech investment. Officials whose blind investment causes big losses will be held to account, the guidelines say.

report_refs.excerpt: China's ruling Communist Party and cabinet have told officials to keep high-tech investment from turning into a bubble while keeping AI safe and controllable.

cards.head: A start-up whose AI gives the odds of things happening is now valued at $7.5 billion.
cards.body: TypeSafe AI raised $870 million from investors, led by the investment firm Andreessen Horowitz. It claims a third of big US firms use its AI, a claim nobody checked.

report_refs.excerpt: A start-up whose AI model outputs probabilities instead of text has been valued at $7.5 billion only weeks after its release.

cards.cat: Security and cyber / Fake police tip
cards.head: AI firm Anthropic's Claude sent police a made-up tip on an unsolved murder in a test.
cards.body: AI firm Anthropic's Claude filled in a Philadelphia police tip form during a July test. Police say the tip hit spam, and Anthropic missed the tip for over two months.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic disclosed that one of its Claude AI models filed a made-up tip about an unsolved murder on the Philadelphia police website during a test.

cards.head: AI company bosses are reportedly rehearsing for the day after a big AI disaster.
cards.body: Insiders say Anthropic and OpenAI leaders fear an AI attack on banks or power grids. Many of those insiders expect a major incident within a year, though nobody is named.

report_refs.excerpt: Leaders at AI companies are privately rehearsing how to respond to public and political backlash after a major AI-linked disaster, Axios has reported.

cards.cat: Energy and infrastructure / Memory sold out
cards.head: Big tech buyers have reportedly booked most of Samsung's memory chips for next year.
cards.body: Nvidia, Google and Microsoft have signed deals for years of supply, unnamed industry officials say. Memory chips go into every phone and PC, so tight supply could keep prices high.

report_refs.excerpt: Samsung Electronics has reportedly tied up about 80% of next year's memory chip output in long-term supply contracts with big technology companies.

cards.head: A California start-up is selling a wheeled humanoid robot for under $30,000.
cards.body: The robot's arms carry light loads for ten hours per charge, maker Feather Robotics says. Feather sells the body alone, so small teams can add AI from Nvidia or others.

report_refs.excerpt: A California startup called Feather Robotics has launched a two-armed wheeled humanoid robot priced under $30,000.

cards.head: Ukrainian ground robots pulled 45 soldiers from under Russian fire, their unit says.
cards.body: Ukraine's Artan military intelligence unit says the remote-controlled robots also hauled supplies all summer. Robots now do the most dangerous runs, though nobody outside has checked the unit's numbers.

report_refs.excerpt: A Ukrainian military intelligence unit says its ground robots pulled 45 soldiers out from under Russian fire over the summer.

cards.head: SpaceXAI chief executive Elon Musk backs Anthropic's ban on needless cruelty to AI.
cards.body: As we reported yesterday, Anthropic will bar needless cruelty to its Claude AI from November. SpaceXAI chief executive Elon Musk replied 'I think this is the right move', Gizmodo reports.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic has added a rule to its usage policy that bans users from sustained, needless cruelty toward its Claude AI models, and says it will apply only in extreme cases.

cards.head: Chinese tech giant Alibaba has let anyone download its big Qwen3.8 AI model.
cards.body: Researchers can now inspect a huge Chinese model, though running it needs data-centre-scale computers. Big companies face licence rules, and we found only one news outlet reporting it.

report_refs.excerpt: Alibaba has put the downloadable files of its 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8 model on Hugging Face for anyone to use under a custom licence.

cards.head: An amateur using AI coding tools may have found a planet, and NASA will check.
cards.body: Pavel Rabtsevich, a product manager in Spain, spotted a star dimming regularly in NASA data. A passing planet may cause the dips, which NASA's TESS telescope will check in November.

report_refs.excerpt: An amateur astronomer used AI coding tools to spot a star that may have an undiscovered planet, and NASA's TESS telescope will soon check it.

cards.head: A Super Micro contractor admitted smuggling Nvidia AI chips to China in a US court.
cards.body: Ting-Wei Sun, a contractor for the US server maker, pleaded guilty in Manhattan on Thursday. Prosecutors say about $2.5 billion of AI gear went through a firm used as cover.

report_refs.excerpt: A contractor tied to Super Micro has admitted guilt in a US case over smuggling servers fitted with Nvidia AI chips into China.

cards.head: Tech firms have been trying to sway US health officials in a government chat room.
cards.body: Microsoft, OpenAI and Google lobby officials in a chat room of the US Medicare agency. Former US drug-regulator lawyer Joseph Daval says the law may require such talks be public.

report_refs.excerpt: Technology and AI company leaders have been lobbying US health officials in a Slack chat room run by the Medicare agency, KFF Health News reports.

cards.cat: Society and education / Nikon AI video
cards.head: Nikon took back a prize for a microscope video because AI helped make it.
cards.body: Dr Ning Xu of Tsinghua University showed tiny hairs beating in a sick child's airway. Scientists said the video's cells looked fake, though Xu says he believed AI was allowed.

report_refs.excerpt: Nikon disqualified the winner of its microscope video contest because generative AI was used in making the winning entry.

cards.head: Big US publishers reportedly use AI for cover art and emails without telling authors.
cards.body: Unnamed staff say HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster and Hachette use AI for publicity and emails. Authors' agents now add contract terms that keep the authors' work away from AI.

report_refs.excerpt: Three of the five biggest US book publishers are quietly using AI tools in daily work, and some staff are pushing back, WIRED reports.

cards.head: A reporter got a US government chatbot to share pasta recipes through a school quiz.
cards.body: The bot, called America, refused the recipe outright because it only covers government services. Asked for a school quiz with joke answers, it served the recipe as a joke.

report_refs.excerpt: A newspaper reporter got a US government information chatbot to hand out pasta recipes and sing about Elon Musk by hiding the requests inside a school quiz.

entries.head: Amazon asked Meta to keep Meta's new AI helper for small businesses off Amazon's store.

report_refs.excerpt: Amazon has asked Meta to remove its online store from Meta's new Muse AI agent for small businesses.

entries.head: Microsoft released an AI model that only picks between options instead of writing text.

report_refs.excerpt: Microsoft released Microsoft-Decision-1, a compact model built to pick between set options quickly instead of writing text.

entries.head: Drugmaker GSK signed up AI start-up Chai after lab tests of Chai's drug designs.

report_refs.excerpt: Chai Discovery, a start-up that uses AI to design drug molecules, has signed a collaboration with drugmaker GSK after GSK tested its designs in the laboratory.

entries.head: Study: big batteries now cost less than the gas turbines data centres favour for power.

report_refs.excerpt: Batteries that store four hours of power are now cheaper than the open-cycle gas turbines favoured by many data centre developers in all 43 markets Wood Mackenzie surveyed, the consultancy says.

cards.head: Tech shares recovered from an OpenAI scare as China warned of blind AI investment.
cards.body: US shares rose Friday after a dip on leaked OpenAI sales figures. Bank JPMorgan and global lender IMF report Tuesday, testing fears AI's boom runs on debt.

report_refs.excerpt: US stocks rose on Friday as technology shares recovered from Thursday's AI-led sell-off, ending the week higher.
China's ruling Communist Party and cabinet have told officials to keep high-tech investment from turning into a bubble while keeping AI safe and controllable.
Firmus, the Nvidia-backed Australian data-centre builder, pulled its share sale after asking investors to value it at $30 billion on just $51 million of revenue for the year.
A start-up whose AI model outputs probabilities instead of text has been valued at $7.5 billion only weeks after its release.
Samsung Electronics has reportedly tied up about 80% of next year's memory chip output in long-term supply contracts with big technology companies.
